newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lamfalussy - realistic chance of punctual EMU start.
newsitem.headline: Lamfalussy - realistic chance of punctual EMU start.

text.p: European Monetary Institute (EMI) President Alexandre Lamfalussy said in a speech on Wednesday that there was a realistic chance that European currency union would start as scheduled on January 1, 1999.

"After assessing all the problems yet to be resolved, there remains a realistic chance of keeping to the timetable for moving to the third stage of monetary union," Lamfalussy said at Karlsruhe University.
Lamfalussy went on to warn the financial markets against an excess of optimism in the run-up to currency union.

"It is equally important to warn against exaggerated optimism in the markets, which led to an excessive kind of convergence euphoria before the European Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) crisis in 1992," Lamfalussy said.

Lamfalussy also said the EMI took a positive view on current discussions by EU finance ministers aimed at producing a stability pact, containing sanctions against EMU member states which do not continue to meet EMU criteria after currency union.
"The council of the EMI considers these efforts to be extremely important and to be welcomed," said Lamfalussy.
Lamfalussy said the EMI will conclude its technical preparations for EMU punctually, so there would be no cause for delay in currency union from that side.

"The convergence process is making advances, which should continue in the coming period. In the end the necessary political will is evident in many countries to make economic and currency union a reality," Lamfalussy said.
